title: Bombay High Court: Pursuing Online Courses on an Employment Visa Does Not Violate Its Conditions Absent an Explicit Bar
case_name: Wu Jyun Lin v. Foreigners Regional Registration Office
citation: 2026 LiveLaw (Bom) 349; Writ Petition (L) No. 8223 of 2026, decided 28 July 2026
card_summary: A Taiwan national working at a Gujarat firm on an employment visa took online courses alongside his job, then moved to a student visa for an LLB in Mumbai. The FRRO closed his representations without reasons, demanded a Rs 50,000 penalty and issued an exit permit. The Bombay HC quashed the order as arbitrary, holding his visa carried only two conditions, neither barring education, so the courses did not breach it.
card_tip: Before penalising a foreign employee for activity outside work, check the conditions actually endorsed on the visa; an FRRO cannot read in a restriction, such as a bar on study, that the visa itself never states.
verification_notes: The Taiwan national's employment in Gujarat, the online HR certification and law courses, the later student visa for an LLB at Government Law College Mumbai, the FRRO's Rs 50,000 penalty demand and exit permit, and the 28 July 2026 Bombay High Court decision (2026 LiveLaw (Bom) 349) quashing that order are corroborated across LiveLaw, Verdictum and Rawlaw reports of the same judgment.
